scope: Same real-poster learned occupancy flow, checkpoint, all 4096 tokens, DINO conditioning, real-pair RoPE, original 12-step/22-forward sampler. QK/scaling/softmax FP32; probabilities and AV use original BF16 torso dtype.
pairing: Original reference-source/checkpoint/config/version/input signatures equal to refreshed FP32 control. Both reuse the same sealed stock FP32 CPU trajectory after physical checkpoint hash and exact fixture checks.
finding: BF16 AV decreases real-poster final latent error vs stock FP32 from 0.6074 to 0.5750. Forward latency is 5824.9ms vs 5886.1ms; complete sampler timings are retained below. This is an exploratory matched run on one crop, not proof of general accuracy or a statistically established small speed gain.
decision: Keep opt-in and strict failed trajectory gates. Assess common-decoder occupancy in result046. Test the independent head-first RoPE layout for larger avoidable layout costs; isolated attention speed savings did not translate into a large full-flow gain.
reference_retention: The shared original CPU payload is retained in result027; device candidate trajectory is retained here. Native returncode1 denotes failed numerical gates, not a runtime failure.
